_note: Synthetic curve sample series. Offsets are MINUTES from the token's first_seen_at; progress is progress_pct. These are CHANGE-ONLY series, exactly as grad_curve_samples stores them: a gap means no reserve moved, not that nothing was looked at. Every expected value in test_features.py was worked out by hand from these numbers.

sparse._note: The change-only case the whole engine has to get right. Long quiet stretches, including a 45-minute one between 91% and 96%. A reader that did not forward-fill would compute velocity from the wrong end of each gap.

retrace._note: Rises to 88%, falls back to 80.5% — a 7.5-point give-back from a running peak — then recovers and graduates. The 70 and 80 checkpoints must flag it; the 90 checkpoint comes AFTER the fall and must not. 95 is never reached, so its whole block is null.

never_reached_90._note: Crosses 70 and 80 and then graduates without ever being SEEN at 90 — the curve filled between two polls. The 90 and 95 blocks are null and the token is still written, because 'reached 80 and died' is the row Phase 3 most needs.

_price_note: Post-graduation prices as [minute_after_graduation, price_usd]. One a minute, as a live 60s poll would produce.

prices_full._note: Opens at 1.0 two minutes after graduation, peaks at 2.5 ten minutes in, bottoms at 0.8, closes at 1.1. Full 60-minute coverage.

prices_thin._note: Only 30 of the 60 minutes carry a sample. Under the 55-minute floor, so every return must be NULL and postgrad_minutes_covered must say why.
